newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: DIPLOMATS SAY RURAL REFORM URGENT.
newsitem.headline: DIPLOMATS SAY RURAL REFORM URGENT.

text.p: Diplomats here say that rural reforms are urgently needed for Lithuania to complete its transition to a market economy and prepare for European Union membership (EU).
"Lithuania's economy is now past the critical juncture...it turned around fundamentally in 1994," Britain's ambassador to Lithuania, Thomas Macan, told Reuters in an interview.
But he said that the agricultural sector, which employs 22 percent of the country's work force, needs to be firmly addresssed.
"Such a high proportion of farm workers can only continue if people are content with a peasant standard of living," Macan said.
The rural population, a third of the total in this historically agricultural nation, has been struggling with market forces since the break-up of the collective farm system in 1992.
The United Nations Development Programme's (UNDP) 1996 report for Lithuania said that rural incomes at the end of 1995 were 29 percent of their 1990 level compared with 40 percent for urban incomes.
Many farmers till their tiny plots with horse-drawn ploughs.

"Agriculture must be dramatically restructured...The units are simply too small to be viable in a market economy," said Henrik Schmiegelow, the head of the European Commission's delegation to Lithuania.
He adds that the coutry's sizable rural population has helped to cusion the impact of its market transformation.
"In a period of transition, agriculture has helped...it has kept people employed, even if in an inefficient way," he said.
As it reaches out to embrace new members from the east, the European Union is concerned about the high costs of subsidies to large and poor rural populations.
"People must be encouraged to leave the land," Macan said.
"Other successful late developing economies like Portugal and Ireland have shown that this can be done," he said.
"Market forces must be allowed to operate...agricultural tariffs and subsidies only prolong the misery," Macan added.
